paragraphs.text: Development kit for DeepSeek Harness plugins: compose a profile, boot a throwaway shadow, verify the
host half, capture the client half, roll back a broken profile
# @citisen/dsh-plugin-dev

Development kit for DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`)
plugins: a small CLI for the parts that must be determi

nistic, and a bundled
agent skill for the judgment in between.

Most dsh plugin failures are not code failures. They are **composition** failures
(a row that does n

ot resolve, a patch that replaces a whole `config`, a provider
id that collides) or **client half**

failures (a bundle that never mounts). None
of those show up in a unit test, and all of them cost an

afternoon when the only
feedback is a broken app.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Why a package and not a script

`dsh` is an order of magnitude easier to develop against when the loop is:
compose → diff → boot → l

ook. That loop is four commands, and each of them is
fiddly in a way that should be solved once:

- the desktop profile is **refused** by the CLI ("managed exclusively by the
Electron application"),

so every check needs a copy;
- the GUI answers **401 without its token**, and readiness is a `303`

ink:` dependency that a package manager replaces can delete the linked
worktree, `.git` included.
The commands encode those; the skill explains when to use which, and why.
## Install
As a bundle, so the agent gets the skill (recommended):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The package registers a skill provider, so `dsh-plugin-dev` appears in the agent
catalog. No other p

rofile row is touched, and disabling the bundle removes it
again.
Standalone, for the CLI without the skill:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Commands
| Command | What it does |
| `doctor` | Detects the launcher and its version, lists profiles, checks whether the chosen profile

composes, finds a Chromium |
| `compose` | Composes a profile through the real launcher. `--save` r

ecords a baseline, `--check` exits 1 on drift, `--json` lists entries and duplicate ids |
| `shadow`
| Copies a profile (files copied, `node_modules` linked), boots it on an OS-assigned port, waits fo

r the URL, probes it, prints url/token/log |
| `shot` | Renders a URL in headless Chromium over CDP:
PNG, DOM stats, console errors and uncaught exceptions. `--fail-on-console-error` makes them fatal

|
| `snapshot` | Saves, lists and restores the three files that decide a profile's composition. `res
tore` snapshots the current state first |
Common flags: `--dsh <path>`, `--json`, `--help`.
## Requirements

- `dsh` — the desktop application (the bundled CLI is found automatically), the
published CLI on `PA

TH`, or `--dsh <path>` / `$DSH_CLI`.
- Node 20+ for the CLI.
- Chromium, Chrome or Edge for `shot` (

found automatically; `--browser <path>` or
`CHROME_PATH` otherwise).
- Windows, macOS and Linux. The
desktop app is optional: any `dsh` works.
## How it works

Nothing is reimplemented. `compose` runs `dsh --profile

--dump-config` and diffs that text; `sha

dow` runs `dsh --profile <copy> --no-open --port 0` and reads
the URL the launcher prints; `shot` dr

ives the browser over the DevTools protocol
and nothing else. When the launcher refuses the desktop

profile, `compose` and
`shadow` build a temporary copy under another name — the same workaround a pe

rson
would do by hand.

The host half is deliberately trivial: it reads `skills/dsh-plugin-dev/SKILL.md`
and registers one s
kill provider. It cannot fail a profile boot.
## Version support

Tested with `dsh 0.2.1-rc.2` on Windows 11 (Electron 44 / Node 24.21). The kit
shells out to the lau

ncher, so a version that changes `--dump-config`, the
`dsh web:` boot line, or the desktop-profile p

olicy will surface as a loud error
from `doctor` rather than a silent wrong answer. Please open an i

ssue with the
`doctor --json` output.
## Contributing

The trap list is the product. See CONTRIBUTING.md — the short
version is: a step becomes a script on

its second manual repetition, and a bug
report becomes an entry in
`skills/dsh-plugin-dev/reference

manual repetition, and a bug
report becomes an entry in
`skills/dsh-plugin-dev/references/traps.md`.
